To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SOI1 encodes a novel protein that promotes cycling of TSN membrane proteins between the Golgi and prevacuole by antagonizing a Golgi retention signal and facilitating a retrieval signal.
SOI1 encodes a novel protein that functions at two steps to promote cycling of TGN proteins between the TGP and prevacuole.

Soi1 protein promotes cycling of TSGN membrane proteins between the Golgi complex and the prevacuolar endosome by antagonizing the function of a Golgi retention signal and by facilitating the function of an endosomal retrieval signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the TGN is organized and how membrane proteins are sorted in this compartment.
the mechanism by which proteins are transported between organelles in the secretory and endocytic pathways.
the sorting and recycling of membrane proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Soi1 protein is required for optimal function and/or stability of the TLS1 and TLS2 signals, which in turn are required for the normal cycling of Kex 2 protease between the TGN, PVC and vacuole.
Soi1 protein promotes TGN localization of proteins by antagonizing the function of TLS2 and facilitating the function TLS1.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Soi1 is a novel protein that promotes TGN–endosomal cycling of Kex proteases and other membrane proteins by modulating two signals in the C-tail.
Soi1 is a novel protein that is required for the cycling of TGN proteins between the TNG and prevacuole.

Soi1 protein promotes TGN-endosome cycling of membrane proteins by antagonizing the function of TGN retention signals (TLS2) that act at TGN and facilitating the function TLS1, the TGN to endosome retrieval signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Soi1 protein promotes TGN-endosomal cycling of TGN proteins by antagonizing TLS2 and facilitating TLS1.

Soi1 protein functions to facilitate the retrieval of Kex2 proteases from the prevacuolar compartments (PVCs) to the trans-Golgi network (TGN) by modulating the function of two signals in the cytosolic tail of Kex2.
